title: Repertoire of the dance band: Whispering, Margie and Dixieland
summary: They played a mix of commercial hits and their own pieces for dancing and kept playing Dixieland jazz even in high-class rooms.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Well, what kind of music then were you playing? Was this dance music, was it Dixieland jazz, or --
We played a mixture of everything.
According to the tunes we'd get. We'd get -- according to the tunes, we'd get, we'd play -- most of the things, started to become commercial. Tunes like
"Whispering," and "Margie." Then we'd play a few of our own compositions, imagination was quite a lot of that, you see.
Our own stuff, and the style of Dixieland.
You did more of a Dixieland concert?
Yes. We had a variety. You could play a variety as long as it's not too loud.
But it was mostly for dancing?

Mostly for dancing. Everything we did was more or less for dancing, after the Syncopated Orchestra. Even on the stage, we did two or three numbers especially arranged, it was an attraction on stage. We had to. But, most of everything we did was dancing.
So you were playing a lot of Dixieland jazz at that time?
Yes, we did. We played a lot of Dixieland jazz and kept on playing Dixieland jazz even in the high spots.
